sentences.text: Phalarodon is recognized by a parietal bone forming a large part of its sagittal crest, a lack of dental groove in the maxilla, and a pronounced shelf around the nostrils.
Research in 2000 revealed that Phalarodon atavus possessed a skull shape indicating it had a very strong bite.
The type specimen of Phalarodon fraasi, consisting of a skull and jaw fragments, was collected by John Campbell Merriam in Nevada and described in 1910.
Fossils of this species have since been found in Guizhou Province, China, and the Botneheia Formation on Svalbard, Norway.
Phalarodon belongs to the subfamily Phalarodontinae within the family Mixosauridae.
In 2004, a reanalysis merged Phalarodon fraasi into the genus Mixosaurus, a classification that was later overturned.
Phalarodon lived during the Middle Triassic period, between 247.2 and 242.0 million years ago.
Phalarodon callawayi and Phalarodon fraasi lived in the same ecosystem as other marine reptiles like the ichthyosaurs Cymbospondylus and Omphalosaurus, and the sauropterygian Augustasaurus.
